newsitem.title: USA: Cross Timbers reserves up 33 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Cross Timbers reserves up 33 pct in 1996.

text.p: Cross Timbers Oil Co said Friday proved oil and natural gas reserves at year-end 1996 were 132.5 million barrels of oil equivalent, a 33 percent increase from the 99.7 million barrels a year earlier.
Natural gas reserves increased 51 percent to 540.54 billion cubic feet. Oil reserves increased six percent to 42.4 million barrels, the company said.
It said most of the natural gas increase came on the purchase of 153.4 billion cubic feet, helped by an upward revesion of previous reserve estimates of 29.38 billion cubic feet.
Cross Timbers said it replaced 438 percent of its 1996 oil and natural gas production of 9.7 million barrels of oil equivalent at a cost of $3.51 per barrel of oil equivalent.
"Growth through acquisitions was supplemented by our development program which alone replaced more than 162 percent of production at an impressive cost of only $2.86 per barrel of oil equivalent."
It said 1996 production included 3.5 million barrels of oil and 37.27 billion cubic feet of natural gas.

Using price and cost assumptions established by the Securities and Exchange Commission, estimated future net cash flows, before income taxes, totaled $1.7 billion at December 31, 1996, Cross Timbers said.

The present value before income tax, discounted at 10 percent, was $946 million, up 133 percent from year-end 1995 levels, based upon 1996 year-end prices of $24.25 per barrel of oil and $3.02 per thousand cubic feet of natural gas.
Barrels of oil equivalent are calculated by dividing billions of cubic feet of natural gas by six and adding that figure to million barrels of crude and natural gas liquids.
